FunctionNodeAlignEulerToVector.node: Turns a rotation (three angles) so one of its axes points along a direction you choose. Use it to make objects face somewhere.

inputs.Rotation: The starting rotation as X, Y, Z angles. This is the rotation that gets turned toward the direction.
inputs.Factor: How much to align. 0 keeps the original rotation, 1 aligns fully, 0.5 goes halfway.
inputs.Vector: The direction to point toward. Only where it points matters, not how long it is.

FunctionNodeAlignRotationToVector.node: Turns a rotation so one of its axes points along a direction you choose. Use it to make instances face a direction or a surface normal.

inputs.Rotation: The starting rotation. This is what gets turned toward the direction.
inputs.Factor: How much to align. 0 keeps the original rotation, 1 aligns fully, 0.5 goes halfway.
inputs.Vector: The direction to point toward. Only where it points matters, not how long it is.

FunctionNodeAxesToRotation.node: Builds a rotation from two directions. The main axis points exactly along the first, the other tries to follow the second.

inputs.Primary Axis: Direction the chosen primary axis must point along. This one is matched exactly.
inputs.Secondary Axis: Direction the second axis tries to match. It is adjusted if it is not at a right angle to the primary.

FunctionNodeAxisAngleToRotation.node: Makes a rotation by spinning around an imaginary pole by an angle, like a door turning on its hinge.

inputs.Axis: The pole to spin around. Only its direction matters, not its length.
inputs.Angle: How far to spin around the pole, in radians. 0 is no turn, 3.14 is half a turn, 6.28 is a full turn.

FunctionNodeBitMath.node: Does math on the individual 0s and 1s (bits) inside whole numbers. Used for flags and advanced tricks.

inputs.A: The first whole number. Its bits are used in the operation.
inputs.B: The second whole number, combined with A bit by bit.
inputs.Shift: How many bit places to slide. Only used by the shift operations. Higher slides the bits further.

FunctionNodeBooleanMath.node: Combines true/false values with logic like AND, OR and NOT. Use it to combine selections.

inputs.Boolean_001: The second true/false value. Ignored by operations that need only one input, like NOT.

FunctionNodeCombineColor.node: Builds one color from separate numbers, using RGB, HSV or HSL. Handy for making colors with math.

inputs.Red: First channel: Red in RGB, Hue in HSV or HSL. 0 is none, 1 is full.
inputs.Green: Second channel: Green in RGB, Saturation in HSV or HSL. 0 is none, 1 is full.
inputs.Blue: Third channel: Blue in RGB, Value in HSV, Lightness in HSL. 0 is none, 1 is full.
inputs.Alpha: How solid the color is. 0 is see-through, 1 is fully solid.

FunctionNodeCombineMatrix.node: Builds a 4x4 grid of numbers (a matrix) from 16 separate values. A matrix stores move, rotate and scale together.

inputs.Column 1 Row 1: Stretch along X when there is no rotation. 1 keeps the size, 2 doubles it.
inputs.Column 1 Row 2: Rotation and tilt mixing (column 1, row 2). Usually 0 unless you want a turned or sheared shape.
inputs.Column 1 Row 3: Rotation and tilt mixing (column 1, row 3). Usually 0 unless you want a turned or sheared shape.
inputs.Column 1 Row 4: Bottom row value. Normally 0; only used for advanced perspective effects.
inputs.Column 2 Row 1: Rotation and tilt mixing (column 2, row 1). Usually 0 unless you want a turned or sheared shape.
inputs.Column 2 Row 2: Stretch along Y when there is no rotation. 1 keeps the size, 2 doubles it.
inputs.Column 2 Row 3: Rotation and tilt mixing (column 2, row 3). Usually 0 unless you want a turned or sheared shape.
inputs.Column 2 Row 4: Bottom row value. Normally 0; only used for advanced perspective effects.
inputs.Column 3 Row 1: Rotation and tilt mixing (column 3, row 1). Usually 0 unless you want a turned or sheared shape.
inputs.Column 3 Row 2: Rotation and tilt mixing (column 3, row 2). Usually 0 unless you want a turned or sheared shape.
inputs.Column 3 Row 3: Stretch along Z when there is no rotation. 1 keeps the size, 2 doubles it.
inputs.Column 3 Row 4: Bottom row value. Normally 0; only used for advanced perspective effects.
inputs.Column 4 Row 1: Movement along X stored in the matrix. Higher values move things farther along X.
inputs.Column 4 Row 2: Movement along Y stored in the matrix. Higher values move things farther along Y.
inputs.Column 4 Row 3: Movement along Z stored in the matrix. Higher values move things farther along Z.
inputs.Column 4 Row 4: Bottom-right corner of the matrix. Normally 1; changing it scales everything.

FunctionNodeCombineTransform.node: Packs a move, a rotation and a scale into one transformation matrix, so you can place geometry with a single value.

inputs.Translation: How far to move along X, Y and Z. 0 means no movement.
inputs.Scale: Size on X, Y and Z. 1 is normal, 2 is double, below 1 shrinks.

FunctionNodeCompare.node: Compares two values and outputs true or false, like 'is A bigger than B'. Great for making selections.

inputs.B: The second value, compared against A.

FunctionNodeEulerToRotation.node: Turns three angles (X, Y, Z) into a rotation value that rotation sockets accept.

inputs.Euler: Three angles in radians, one per axis. 0 is no turn, 3.14 is half a turn.

FunctionNodeFindInString.node: Counts how many times a piece of text appears inside another text and tells where the first match starts.

inputs.Search: The text you are looking for.
inputs.Mode: A menu that picks how the search is done. Choose an option from the list.

FunctionNodeFloatToInt.node: Turns a decimal number into a whole number. You pick how: round, floor, ceiling or truncate.

inputs.Float: The decimal number to convert. For example 2.7 becomes 3 when rounding and 2 when flooring.

FunctionNodeFormatString.node: Builds text from a template by dropping values into it, like 'Count: {n}'. Add an input for each name in braces.

inputs.Format: The template text. Put a name in curly braces, like {Count}, where a value should appear.

FunctionNodeHashValue.node: Turns a number into a random-looking whole number. The same input always gives the same output.

inputs.Value: The number to scramble. The same value always gives the same result.
inputs.Seed: Changes the scrambling. A different seed gives a different pattern.

FunctionNodeInputBool.node: Gives a single true/false value you set with a checkbox. Plug it into any node that needs a yes/no.

FunctionNodeInputColor.node: Gives a color you choose with the color picker. Plug it into any color input.

FunctionNodeInputInt.node: Gives a whole number that you type in. Plug it into any integer input.

FunctionNodeInputIntVector.node: Gives three whole numbers (X, Y, Z) that you type in, such as grid sizes.

FunctionNodeInputMenu.node: Gives a menu choice you can plug into menu inputs on other nodes, so one switch controls many nodes.

FunctionNodeInputRotation.node: Gives a rotation that you set by typing angles. Plug it into any rotation input.

FunctionNodeInputSpecialCharacters.node: Gives text characters you cannot easily type, like a line break or a tab. Use it when building text.

FunctionNodeInputString.node: Gives a piece of text that you type in. Plug it into any text input.

FunctionNodeInputVector.node: Gives three numbers (X, Y, Z) that you type in. Use it for positions, directions or sizes.

FunctionNodeIntegerMath.node: Does math on whole numbers: add, subtract, multiply, divide, power and more. Results stay whole numbers.

inputs.Value_001: The second whole number. Some operations ignore it.
inputs.Value_002: The third whole number. Only used by operations with three inputs, like Multiply Add.

FunctionNodeInvertMatrix.node: Finds the matrix that undoes the given one. Use it to get back from a moved or turned space to the original.

inputs.Matrix: The matrix to reverse. If it squashes space flat it cannot be reversed, and Invertible turns false.

FunctionNodeInvertRotation.node: Makes the rotation that undoes the given one, like turning the same amount the opposite way.

FunctionNodeMatchString.node: Checks if a text starts with, ends with or contains another text. Outputs true or false.

inputs.Operation: A menu to choose the test: starts with, ends with, or contains.
inputs.Key: The text you are looking for inside the first text.

FunctionNodeMatrixDeterminant.node: Computes one number from a matrix that tells how much it scales volume. Negative means mirrored, 0 means squashed flat.

FunctionNodeMatrixMultiply.node: Combines two matrices into one that does both transformations. Order matters, the right matrix is applied first.

inputs.Matrix: The left matrix. It is applied second.
inputs.Matrix_001: The right matrix. It is applied first.

FunctionNodeMatrixSVD.node: Splits a matrix into a turn, a stretch and another turn. Advanced tool for separating rotation from squash and stretch.

inputs.Matrix: The matrix to split. Only its 3x3 rotation and scale part is used, not the movement.

FunctionNodeProjectPoint.node: Moves a point through a matrix with perspective, like how a camera flattens a 3D point onto a screen.

inputs.Transform: The matrix used to move, turn, scale and apply perspective to the point.

FunctionNodeQuaternionToRotation.node: Builds a rotation from four numbers called a quaternion (W, X, Y, Z), another compact way to store rotations.

inputs.W: The main part of the quaternion. 1 with X, Y and Z at 0 means no rotation.
inputs.X: The X part of the quaternion. Together with Y and Z it sets the turning axis.
inputs.Y: The Y part of the quaternion. Together with X and Z it sets the turning axis.
inputs.Z: The Z part of the quaternion. Together with X and Y it sets the turning axis.

FunctionNodeRandomValue.node: Makes a random number, vector, color or true/false. Each element can get its own different value.

inputs.Min: The lowest value the random result can be.
inputs.Max: The highest value the random result can be.
inputs.ID: Picks which random value each element gets. By default it is the element's index, so each one differs.
inputs.Seed: Changes the whole random pattern. Any new number gives a different but repeatable result.

FunctionNodeReplaceString.node: Finds a piece of text and swaps it for another everywhere it appears.

inputs.Find: The piece of text to look for.
inputs.Replace: The text to put in place of each match.

FunctionNodeReverseString.node: Flips the order of the letters in a text, so 'abc' becomes 'cba'.

FunctionNodeRotateEuler.node: Adds a second turn onto a rotation given as angles. You choose whether the extra turn is global or local.

inputs.Rotation: The starting rotation, as X, Y, Z angles.
inputs.Rotate By: The extra turn to add, as X, Y, Z angles.

FunctionNodeRotateRotation.node: Adds a second rotation on top of a first one. You choose whether the extra turn is global or local.

inputs.Rotate By: The extra rotation to add on top.

FunctionNodeRotateVector.node: Spins a vector (a position or direction) around the center by a rotation.

inputs.Vector: The position or direction to spin.

FunctionNodeRotationToAxisAngle.node: Splits a rotation into the pole it spins around and how far it spins.

FunctionNodeRotationToEuler.node: Turns a rotation into three angles (X, Y, Z) you can read or change with math.

FunctionNodeRotationToQuaternion.node: Reads out the four quaternion numbers (W, X, Y, Z) that describe a rotation.

FunctionNodeSeparateColor.node: Splits a color into separate numbers: red/green/blue, hue/saturation/value, or hue/saturation/lightness.

inputs.Color: The color to split into channels.

FunctionNodeSeparateMatrix.node: Splits a 4x4 matrix into its 16 individual numbers.

FunctionNodeSeparateTransform.node: Splits a transformation matrix into its move, its rotation and its scale.

FunctionNodeSetStringCase.node: Changes text to all capital letters or all small letters.

inputs.Case: A menu choosing upper case or lower case.

FunctionNodeSliceString.node: Cuts out a part of a text, starting at a position and keeping a number of characters.

inputs.Position: Where to start cutting. 0 is the first character.
inputs.Length: How many characters to keep. Higher keeps more of the text.

FunctionNodeSplitString.node: Cuts a text into a list of pieces wherever a separator appears, like splitting 'a,b,c' at the commas.

inputs.Separator: The text that marks where to cut, such as a comma.

FunctionNodeStringLength.node: Counts how many characters are in a text.

FunctionNodeStringToValue.node: Reads a number out of a text, like turning the text '42' into the number 42.

inputs.Base: The number system used to read the text. 10 is normal, 2 is binary, 16 is hexadecimal.

FunctionNodeTransformDirection.node: Applies a matrix's turn and scale to a direction. Movement is ignored, since directions have no place.

inputs.Transform: The matrix to apply. Its movement part is ignored.

FunctionNodeTransformPoint.node: Applies a full matrix (move, turn and scale) to a point and gives its new place.

FunctionNodeTransposeMatrix.node: Flips a matrix over its diagonal so columns become rows and rows become columns.

FunctionNodeTrimString.node: Removes unwanted characters from the start and end of a text, like extra spaces.

inputs.Characters: The specific characters to remove from the edges.
inputs.Whitespace: If on, also removes spaces, tabs and line breaks at the edges.
inputs.Start: If on, trims the beginning of the text.
inputs.End: If on, trims the end of the text.

FunctionNodeValueToString.node: Turns a number into text, so it can be shown or joined with other text.

inputs.Value: The number to turn into text.
inputs.Decimals: How many digits to show after the decimal point. 0 gives a whole number, higher shows more detail.
inputs.Base: The number system for the text. 10 is normal, 2 is binary, 16 is hexadecimal.
inputs.Padding: Minimum length of the text. Shorter results are padded at the front. 0 means no padding.

GeometryNodeAccumulateField.node: Makes a running total of a field. Each element gets the sum of all earlier values plus its own, like counting up a tab.

inputs.Value: The value to add up along the elements.
inputs.Group Index: Elements with the same ID are totaled separately. Leave it empty to total everything together.

GeometryNodeAttributeDomainSize.node: Counts how many points, edges, faces, corners, curves or instances a geometry has. Use it to know how big something is.

GeometryNodeAttributeStatistic.node: Measures a field over a geometry: average, middle value, sum, smallest, biggest, range and spread.

inputs.Selection: Only selected elements are included in the measurement.
inputs.Attribute: The values to measure, for example height or distance.

GeometryNodeBake.node: Saves the incoming data so it is not recalculated every time. Speeds up heavy setups and can store a simulation or animation.

GeometryNodeBlurAttribute.node: Smooths a value by mixing each element with its neighbors, like a blur filter in a photo editor.

inputs.Iterations: How many times the blur repeats. Low is a light smoothing, high is very smooth.
inputs.Weight: How strongly each element pulls on its neighbors. Higher counts more, 0 means it is ignored.

GeometryNodeBoneInfo.node: Reads details about one bone of an armature (a skeleton), like its position, rotation and length.

inputs.Armature: The armature object that contains the bone.
inputs.Bone Name: The exact name of the bone to look up.

GeometryNodeBoundBox.node: Finds the smallest box that fits around a geometry and makes it as a mesh. Also gives the box's min and max corners.

inputs.Use Radius: If on, the thickness of points and curves is counted when sizing the box.

GeometryNodeCameraInfo.node: Reads a camera's settings, like focal length, sensor size and clipping distances.

GeometryNodeCaptureAttribute.node: Freezes a field's values on a geometry so they can be used later, even after the geometry changes.

inputs.Selection: Chooses which elements the values are captured for.

GeometryNodeClosureToList.node: Runs a closure (a small reusable node recipe) many times and collects the results into a list.

inputs.Count: How many times to run the closure. This is also the length of the list.
inputs.Closure: The closure to run for each item.

GeometryNodeClusterByConnected.node: Gives the same ID number to mesh vertices that are joined by edges and are close enough to each other.

inputs.Selection: Chooses which elements are affected. True means the element is used, false means it is left alone.
inputs.Position: The positions used to measure distance. Usually the vertex positions.
inputs.Distance: Largest gap between linked vertices that still counts as one cluster. Low gives many small clusters, high gives few big ones.

GeometryNodeClusterByDistance.node: Groups nearby elements by giving them the same ID number. Use it to find clumps of points.

inputs.Selection: Chooses which elements are affected. True means the element is used, false means it is left alone.
inputs.Group ID: Elements only cluster with others that have the same group ID.
inputs.Position: The positions used to measure distance between elements.
inputs.Distance: Elements closer than this join the same cluster. Low gives many small clusters, high gives few big ones.

GeometryNodeCollectionChildren.node: Lists the objects and sub-collections inside a collection, in name order.

inputs.Recursive: If on, also includes what is inside the sub-collections.

GeometryNodeCollectionInfo.node: Brings in the objects of a collection as instances, so you can place or copy them with nodes.

inputs.Separate Children: If on, each object stays its own instance. If off, they come in as one combined instance.
inputs.Reset Children: If on, each object's own position and rotation are cleared so they sit at the origin.

GeometryNodeConvexHull.node: Wraps a tight shape around all points of the geometry, like cling film, using the fewest faces possible.

GeometryNodeCornersOfEdge.node: For each edge, finds one of the face corners attached to it. A corner is where a face meets a vertex.

inputs.Edge Index: Which edge to look at. By default each edge uses its own index.
inputs.Weights: Used to sort the corners. Lower weights come first.
inputs.Sort Index: Which corner to pick from the sorted list. 0 is the first one.

GeometryNodeCornersOfFace.node: For each face, finds one of the corners that make it up. A corner is where the face meets a vertex.

inputs.Face Index: Which face to look at. By default each face uses its own index.
inputs.Weights: Used to sort the corners. Lower weights come first.
inputs.Sort Index: Which corner to pick from the sorted list. 0 is the first one.

GeometryNodeCornersOfVertex.node: For each vertex, finds one of the face corners attached to it.

inputs.Vertex Index: Which vertex to look at. By default each vertex uses its own index.
inputs.Weights: Used to sort the corners. Lower weights come first.
inputs.Sort Index: Which corner to pick from the sorted list. 0 is the first one.

GeometryNodeCubeGridTopology.node: Makes an on/off 3D grid of voxels (3D pixels) inside a box. It is used as a shape guide for Field to Grid.

inputs.Bounds Min: The lower corner of the box the grid fills.
inputs.Bounds Max: The upper corner of the box the grid fills.
inputs.Resolution X: Number of voxels along X. Higher gives finer detail but is heavier to calculate.
inputs.Resolution Y: Number of voxels along Y. Higher gives finer detail but is heavier to calculate.
inputs.Resolution Z: Number of voxels along Z. Higher gives finer detail but is heavier to calculate.
inputs.Min X: Starting voxel index along X. Shifts the grid's start position in whole voxels.
inputs.Min Y: Starting voxel index along Y. Shifts the grid's start position in whole voxels.
inputs.Min Z: Starting voxel index along Z. Shifts the grid's start position in whole voxels.

GeometryNodeCurveArc.node: Makes a curved arc, either from three points or from a radius and angles. Use it for rounded paths and bends.

inputs.Resolution: How many points make up the curve. Low looks blocky and angular, high looks smooth.
inputs.Start: First point of the arc (Points mode).
inputs.Middle: A point the arc passes through (Points mode).
inputs.End: Last point of the arc (Points mode).
inputs.Radius: Size of the circle the arc is cut from. Higher makes a wider, gentler curve.
inputs.Start Angle: Where the arc begins around the circle, in radians.
inputs.Sweep Angle: How much of the circle the arc covers, in radians. 3.14 is half a circle, 6.28 is a full circle.
inputs.Offset Angle: Extra angle that shifts the arc along the circle (Points mode).
inputs.Connect Center: If on, adds lines from the arc's ends to its center, making a pie slice.
inputs.Invert Arc: If on, draws the other part of the circle instead.

GeometryNodeCurveEndpointSelection.node: Selects the points at the start and end of each curve. Use it to treat the tips differently.

inputs.Start Size: How many points to select from the start of each curve. 0 selects none.
inputs.End Size: How many points to select from the end of each curve. 0 selects none.

GeometryNodeCurveHandleTypeSelection.node: Selects Bezier points based on their handle type (Auto, Vector, Align or Free).

GeometryNodeCurveLength.node: Gives the total length of all the curves added together.

GeometryNodeCurveOfPoint.node: For a control point, tells you which curve it belongs to and where it sits in that curve.

inputs.Point Index: Which control point to look up. By default each point uses its own index.

GeometryNodeCurvePrimitiveBezierSegment.node: Makes a smooth Bezier curve from two end points and two handles that bend it.

inputs.Resolution: How many points make up the curve. Low looks blocky and angular, high looks smooth.
inputs.Start Handle: Handle at the start. Pulls the curve's beginning toward it.
inputs.End Handle: Handle at the end. Pulls the curve's finish toward it.

GeometryNodeCurvePrimitiveCircle.node: Makes a circle curve, either from a radius or from three points it passes through.

inputs.Resolution: How many points make up the curve. Low looks blocky and angular, high looks smooth.
inputs.Point 1: First point the circle passes through (Points mode).
inputs.Point 2: Second point the circle passes through (Points mode).
inputs.Point 3: Third point the circle passes through (Points mode).
inputs.Radius: Size of the circle. Higher makes a bigger circle.

GeometryNodeCurvePrimitiveLine.node: Makes a straight line, either between two points or from a start point in a direction.

inputs.Direction: Which way the line points (Direction mode).
inputs.Length: How long the line is (Direction mode). Higher makes a longer line.

GeometryNodeCurvePrimitiveQuadrilateral.node: Makes a four-sided shape such as a rectangle, trapezoid or kite, or a quad from four points.

inputs.Offset: Slides the top edge sideways compared with the bottom edge.
inputs.Bottom Height: Height of the lower part, from the middle to the bottom corner (Kite mode).
inputs.Top Height: Height of the upper part, from the middle to the top corner (Kite mode).

GeometryNodeCurveQuadraticBezier.node: Makes a smooth curved line from a start, an end, and a middle point that pulls the curve toward it.

inputs.Resolution: How many points make up the curve. Low looks blocky and angular, high looks smooth.
inputs.Middle: A control point that pulls the curve toward it. The curve usually does not touch it.

GeometryNodeCurveSetHandles.node: Sets the handle type (Auto, Vector, Align or Free) for the selected Bezier control points.

inputs.Selection: Chooses which elements are affected. True means the element is used, false means it is left alone.

GeometryNodeCurveSpiral.node: Makes a spiral curve that winds around while rising or shrinking. Use it for springs and swirls.

inputs.Resolution: Points per turn. Low looks angular, high looks smooth.
inputs.Rotations: How many full turns the spiral makes. Higher gives more coils.
inputs.Start Radius: Width of the spiral at its start.
inputs.End Radius: Width of the spiral at its end.
inputs.Height: How tall the spiral is from start to end.
inputs.Reverse: If on, the spiral winds the opposite way.

GeometryNodeCurveSplineType.node: Changes selected curves to another type: Poly, Bezier, NURBS or Catmull Rom.

inputs.Selection: Chooses which elements are affected. True means the element is used, false means it is left alone.

GeometryNodeCurveStar.node: Makes a star-shaped curve by joining points on an inner and an outer circle.

inputs.Points: How many tips the star has. Higher gives a spikier, rounder star.
inputs.Inner Radius: Distance of the inner points from the center. Low makes sharp spikes.
inputs.Outer Radius: Distance of the tips from the center. Higher makes a bigger star.
inputs.Twist: Rotates the inner points relative to the tips, giving a swirled star.

GeometryNodeCurveToMesh.node: Turns curves into a mesh, optionally with a profile shape swept along them. This is how you make pipes and tubes.

inputs.Scale: Size of the profile along the curve. 1 is normal, below 1 makes it thinner, above 1 thicker.
inputs.Fill Caps: If on, closes the open ends of the tube when the profile is a closed shape.

GeometryNodeCurveToPoints.node: Makes points along curves at chosen spots. Use it to place objects along a path.

inputs.Count: How many points per curve (Count mode). Higher gives more points.
inputs.Length: Distance between points (Length mode). Lower gives more points.

GeometryNodeCurvesToGreasePencil.node: Converts curves into Grease Pencil layers, so they can be drawn as strokes.

inputs.Selection: Chooses which elements are affected. True means the element is used, false means it is left alone.
inputs.Instances as Layers: If on, each top-level instance becomes its own Grease Pencil layer.

GeometryNodeDeformCurvesOnSurface.node: Moves and turns hair-like curves to follow a surface when the surface is deformed, such as by shape keys or armatures.

GeometryNodeDeleteGeometry.node: Removes the selected parts of a geometry. You choose whether to delete points, edges, faces and so on.

inputs.Selection: Elements that are true are deleted. False ones stay.

GeometryNodeDistributePointsInGrid.node: Scatters points inside a volume grid, more where the grid values are high.

inputs.Grid: The volume grid that decides where points can appear.
inputs.Density: Points per cubic meter (Random mode). Higher gives more points.
inputs.Seed: Changes the random pattern. Any new number gives a different but repeatable result.
inputs.Spacing: Distance between points along X, Y and Z (Grid mode). Lower gives more points.
inputs.Threshold: Cells with a value below this get no points. Higher keeps only the densest regions.

GeometryNodeDistributePointsInVolume.node: Scatters points inside a volume, either randomly or in an even grid.

inputs.Mode: A menu to choose random scattering or a regular grid.
inputs.Density: Points per cubic meter (Random mode). Higher gives more points.
inputs.Seed: Changes the random pattern. Any new number gives a different but repeatable result.
inputs.Spacing: Distance between points along X, Y and Z (Grid mode). Lower gives more points.
inputs.Threshold: Parts of the volume with a value below this get no points. Higher keeps only denser parts.

GeometryNodeDistributePointsOnFaces.node: Scatters points over the surface of a mesh. Use it for grass, rocks, or anything spread on a surface.

inputs.Distance Min: Smallest allowed gap between points (Poisson mode). Higher spaces them farther apart.
inputs.Density Max: Most points allowed per square meter (Poisson mode). Higher allows tighter packing.
inputs.Density: Points per square meter (Random mode). Higher gives more points.
inputs.Density Factor: Scales the density per face. 0 gives no points, 1 gives the full amount.
inputs.Seed: Changes the random pattern. Any new number gives a different but repeatable result.

GeometryNodeDualMesh.node: Swaps faces and vertices. Each face becomes a vertex and each vertex becomes a face. Triangles turn into hexagon-like shapes.

inputs.Keep Boundaries: If on, edges along the mesh border are kept so the outline stays the same.

GeometryNodeDuplicateElements.node: Makes copies of the selected points, edges, faces, curves or instances.

inputs.Selection: Chooses which elements are affected. True means the element is used, false means it is left alone.
inputs.Amount: How many copies each selected element gets. 0 gives none, higher gives more.

GeometryNodeEdgePathsToCurves.node: Turns paths that follow mesh edges into curves. Each path ends at a start vertex.

inputs.Next Vertex Index: For each vertex, the index of the next vertex along the path.

GeometryNodeEdgePathsToSelection.node: Selects the edges that lie along paths following the mesh edges.

inputs.Next Vertex Index: For each vertex, the index of the next vertex along the path.

GeometryNodeEdgesOfCorner.node: Gives the two edges on either side of a face corner.

inputs.Corner Index: Which face corner to look at. By default each corner uses its own index.

GeometryNodeEdgesOfVertex.node: Finds one of the edges connected to a vertex, and how many edges it has.

inputs.Vertex Index: Which vertex to look at. By default each vertex uses its own index.
inputs.Weights: Used to sort the edges. Lower weights come first.
inputs.Sort Index: Which edge to pick from the sorted list. 0 is the first one.

GeometryNodeEdgesToFaceGroups.node: Splits the faces of a mesh into regions fenced in by the chosen boundary edges. Each region gets an ID.

inputs.Boundary Edges: Edges that act as walls between regions. True means the edge separates regions.

GeometryNodeExtrudeMesh.node: Pushes selected parts of a mesh outward to make new geometry, like pulling a box out of a face.

inputs.Selection: Chooses which elements are affected. True means the element is used, false means it is left alone.
inputs.Offset: Direction and distance of the push. By default it follows each face's normal.
inputs.Offset Scale: Multiplies the push distance. 0 adds no height, higher pushes farther, negative pushes inward.
inputs.Individual: If on, each face is extruded on its own instead of as one connected piece.

GeometryNodeFaceOfCorner.node: Tells you which face a face corner belongs to, and the corner's position inside that face.

inputs.Corner Index: Which face corner to look at. By default each corner uses its own index.

GeometryNodeFieldAtIndex.node: Reads a field's value at a chosen element number, so one element can look at another.

inputs.Value: The field whose value you want to read.
inputs.Index: The number of the element to read from.

GeometryNodeFieldAverage.node: Calculates the mean and the median of a field. The mean is the usual average.

inputs.Group Index: Elements with the same ID are averaged separately. Leave empty to average everything.

GeometryNodeFieldMinAndMax.node: Finds the smallest and biggest values of a field.

inputs.Group Index: Elements with the same ID are checked separately. Leave empty to check everything.

GeometryNodeFieldOnDomain.node: Converts a field to another domain (points, edges, faces, corners), for example reading face values at points.

inputs.Value: The field to carry over to the other domain.

GeometryNodeFieldToGrid.node: Builds volume grids by calculating field values at every active voxel of an existing grid shape.

inputs.Topology: A grid whose active voxels set the shape of the new grids.

GeometryNodeFieldToList.node: Calculates a field a number of times and collects the results into a list.

inputs.Count: How many items the list has. Higher gives a longer list.

GeometryNodeFieldVariance.node: Calculates the standard deviation and variance of a field. Both tell how spread out the values are.

inputs.Group Index: Elements with the same ID are measured separately. Leave empty to measure everything.

GeometryNodeFillCurve.node: Fills the inside of closed curves with flat faces on the XY plane.

inputs.Group ID: Curves with the same ID are filled together as one shape.
inputs.Mode: A menu: fill with triangles or with n-gon faces.
inputs.Fill Rule: A menu that decides how overlapping curves are filled: Even-Odd leaves holes, Non-Zero fills overlaps.

GeometryNodeFilletCurve.node: Rounds the corners of curves by adding circular arcs at the control points.

inputs.Radius: How round the corners become. 0 keeps them sharp, higher rounds them more.
inputs.Limit Radius: If on, the radius is lowered where needed so the arcs do not overlap.
inputs.Mode: A menu: Bezier or Poly rounding.
inputs.Count: Points per rounded corner (Poly mode). Higher is smoother.

GeometryNodeFilterList.node: Removes items from a list. Only items marked true in the selection are kept.

inputs.Selection: True keeps the item, false removes it.

GeometryNodeFlipFaces.node: Reverses the direction a face points (its normal). Use it when a surface looks inside out.

inputs.Selection: Chooses which elements are affected. True means the element is used, false means it is left alone.

GeometryNodeForeachGeometryElementInput.node: Start of a loop that runs the nodes inside once for every point, edge, face and so on.

inputs.Selection: Only the selected elements go through the loop.

GeometryNodeForeachGeometryElementOutput.node: End of a loop that runs the nodes inside once for every element, then collects the results.

GeometryNodeGeometryToInstance.node: Turns each input geometry into an instance. This is often much faster than joining them.

GeometryNodeGetAttributeNames.node: Gets a list of the attribute names on a geometry, optionally filtered by type or domain.

inputs.Filter Data Type: If on, only attributes of the chosen data type are listed.
inputs.Data Type: A menu for the data type to filter by, such as Float or Vector.
inputs.Filter Domain: If on, only attributes on the chosen domain are listed.
inputs.Domain: A menu for the domain to filter by, such as Point or Face.

GeometryNodeGetGeometryBundle.node: Pulls the bundle (a package of named values) out of a geometry.

inputs.Remove: If on, the picked part is also removed from the geometry output, so it is not left in twice.

GeometryNodeGetGeometryComponent.node: Picks out one type of geometry (mesh, curves, point cloud and so on) from a mixed geometry.

inputs.Type: A menu to choose which component to take out.
inputs.Remove: If on, the picked part is also removed from the geometry output, so it is not left in twice.

GeometryNodeGetNamedGrid.node: Gets one volume grid from a volume by its name.

inputs.Name: The exact name of the grid to get.
inputs.Remove: If on, the picked part is also removed from the geometry output, so it is not left in twice.

GeometryNodeGizmoDial.node: Shows a dial in the 3D viewport that you can drag to change a value, like an angle.

inputs.Value: The value the dial controls. Dragging the dial changes it.
inputs.Position: Where the dial sits in the viewport.
inputs.Up: The direction the dial's rotation axis points.
inputs.Screen Space: If on, the dial is drawn facing the screen.
inputs.Radius: Size of the dial. Higher makes a bigger dial.

GeometryNodeGizmoLinear.node: Shows an arrow in the 3D viewport that you can drag to change a value.

inputs.Value: The value the arrow controls. Dragging it changes the value.
inputs.Direction: The direction the arrow points and moves along.

GeometryNodeGizmoTransform.node: Shows move, rotate and scale handles in the viewport for changing a transform.

inputs.Value: The transformation matrix the handles control.

GeometryNodeGreasePencilToCurves.node: Converts Grease Pencil layers into curve instances.

inputs.Selection: Chooses which elements are affected. True means the element is used, false means it is left alone.
inputs.Layers as Instances: If on, each layer becomes its own instance.

GeometryNodeGridAdvect.node: Moves grid values along a velocity field, like smoke carried by wind.

inputs.Grid: The grid whose values are moved.
inputs.Velocity: A vector grid giving the direction and speed of the flow.
inputs.Time Step: How far in time to move. Small is gentle and accurate, large moves farther but gets less accurate.
inputs.Integration Scheme: A menu for how the movement is calculated. More advanced options are more accurate but slower.
inputs.Limiter: A menu for how overshooting values are kept in check.

GeometryNodeGridClip.node: Switches off voxels outside a box. Their values go back to the background value.

GeometryNodeGridCurl.node: Measures how much a vector grid swirls around each point, and the swirl direction.

inputs.Grid: A vector grid, such as a velocity field.

GeometryNodeGridDilateAndErode.node: Grows or shrinks the active area of a grid. Only which voxels are active changes, not their values.

inputs.Grid: The grid to grow or shrink.
inputs.Connectivity: A menu for which neighbors count: faces only, or also edges and corners.
inputs.Tiles: A menu for how big blocks of voxels (tiles) are handled.
inputs.Steps: How many voxels to grow or shrink by. Positive grows the area, negative shrinks it.

GeometryNodeGridDivergence.node: Measures the flow into and out of each point of a vector grid. Positive means flowing out.

inputs.Grid: A vector grid, such as a velocity field.

GeometryNodeGridGradient.node: Finds the direction and strength of the steepest change in a number grid, like the slope on a map.

GeometryNodeGridInfo.node: Reads facts about a volume grid, such as its transform and background value.

GeometryNodeGridLaplacian.node: Measures how much each value differs from the average of its neighbors. Used for smoothing and fluid math.

GeometryNodeGridMean.node: Smooths a grid by replacing each voxel with the average of its surroundings, like a box blur.

inputs.Width: How far around each voxel to average. Higher blurs more.
inputs.Iterations: How many times to repeat the blur. Higher is smoother.

GeometryNodeGridMedian.node: Smooths a grid by replacing each voxel with the middle value of its surroundings. Keeps edges sharper than a mean blur.

inputs.Width: How far around each voxel to look. Higher smooths more.
inputs.Iterations: How many times to repeat. Higher is smoother.

GeometryNodeGridPrune.node: Makes a grid use less memory by merging areas of equal values into larger blocks.

inputs.Grid: The grid to shrink in memory.
inputs.Mode: A menu for how values are judged as equal: exactly, within a threshold, or by inactive state.
inputs.Threshold: Values closer together than this count as equal and get merged. Higher saves more memory but loses detail.

GeometryNodeGridToMesh.node: Makes a mesh along the surface of a volume grid, where the values cross a chosen level.

inputs.Grid: The grid to turn into a surface.
inputs.Threshold: The value at which the surface forms. Raising it shrinks the shape, lowering it grows it.
inputs.Adaptivity: How much the mesh simplifies. 0 keeps full detail, higher gives fewer faces.

GeometryNodeGridToPoints.node: Makes a point for each active voxel of a grid.

inputs.Grid: The grid whose active voxels become points.

GeometryNodeGridVoxelize.node: Turns big active blocks (tiles) of a grid into individual voxels, making the grid fully detailed. Uses more memory.

GeometryNodeImageInfo.node: Reads facts about an image, such as its width, height and number of frames.

inputs.Frame: Which frame to read from, for animated images or sequences.

GeometryNodeImageTexture.node: Reads the color of an image at a chosen spot. Use it to drive geometry with a picture.

inputs.Vector: Where in the image to read (UV style, 0 to 1). By default it uses the element's position.
inputs.Frame: Which frame to read, for animated images or sequences.

GeometryNodeImportCSV.node: Loads a CSV table file (rows and columns of numbers or text) as a point cloud of data.

inputs.Path: Location of the file on your disk. It must point to a real file.
inputs.Delimiter: The character that separates columns in the file, usually a comma.

GeometryNodeImportOBJ.node: Loads a 3D model from an OBJ file as geometry.

inputs.Path: Location of the file on your disk. It must point to a real file.

GeometryNodeImportPLY.node: Loads a point cloud from a PLY file.

inputs.Path: Location of the file on your disk. It must point to a real file.

GeometryNodeImportSTL.node: Loads a mesh from an STL file, often used for 3D printing.

inputs.Path: Location of the file on your disk. It must point to a real file.

GeometryNodeImportText.node: Loads the text inside a text file as a string.

inputs.Path: Location of the file on your disk. It must point to a real file.

GeometryNodeImportVDB.node: Loads volume data (smoke, clouds, fog) from a .vdb file.

inputs.Path: Location of the file on your disk. It must point to a real file.

GeometryNodeIndexOfNearest.node: For each element, finds the closest other element and its index. Use it to link neighbors.

inputs.Position: The positions used to measure distance. Usually the element positions.
inputs.Group ID: Only elements with the same group ID are compared with each other.

GeometryNodeIndexSwitch.node: Picks one of several values using a number. Index 0 gives the first value, 1 the second, and so on.

inputs.Index: Which value to output. Out-of-range numbers use the nearest valid choice.
inputs.Item_0: The value used when the index is 0.
inputs.Item_1: The value used when the index is 1.

GeometryNodeInputActiveCamera.node: Gives the camera that is currently active in the scene.

GeometryNodeInputCollection.node: Gives a single collection you choose from a dropdown.

GeometryNodeInputCurveHandlePositions.node: Reads the positions of the two handles on each Bezier control point.

inputs.Relative: If on, positions are measured from the control point. If off, they are in object space.

GeometryNodeInputCurveTilt.node: Reads the twist angle at each curve point. Tilt rotates the curve's surface around its direction.

GeometryNodeInputEdgeSmooth.node: Tells whether each edge is marked smooth. Smooth edges blend shading, sharp ones show a crease.

GeometryNodeInputFont.node: Gives a font you choose, for use with text nodes.

GeometryNodeInputID.node: Gives each point its stable ID number, which stays the same even if points are deleted or reordered.

GeometryNodeInputImage.node: Gives an image you choose from your loaded images.
